그 성의 밭과 향리는 여분네의 아들 갈렙에게 주었으며
아론 자손에게 도피성을 주었으니 헤브론과 립나와 그 들과 얏딜과 에스드모아와 그 들과
힐렌과 그 들과 드빌과 그 들과
아산과 그 들과 벧세메스와 그 들이며
또 베냐민 지파 중에서는 게바와 그 들과 알레멧과 그 들과 아나돗과 그 들을 주었으니 그핫 족속의 얻은 성이 모두 열셋이었더라

Early settlement scenes use modest Bronze/early Iron Age Canaanite towns, sacred tent at Shiloh, no Solomon temple before it is built. Monarchic Jerusalem grows later; northern Samaria, Phoenicia and Assyria remain distinct. No Roman buildings, medieval armor, modern objects, invented readable Hebrew or map labels. Sacred-object reconstructions are restrained approximations, not archaeological certainty.
Named biblical people are wholly original ancient Near Eastern actors with plausible olive/brown skin, period clothing, and stable identifying features. Joshua continues Torah's original dark-curled, short-bearded sage-mantled man, visibly older during Canaan entry and very elderly at final assembly. ONLY when named Eleazar is actually depicted: one distinct older HIGH priest in blue ephod with exactly twelve breastpiece stones in FOUR rows of THREE. All ordinary ark bearers and horn players wear plain undyed white linen and plain white headwraps: NO breastpieces, gemstones, blue ephods or duplicated high-priest costumes. Never assign high-priest attire to unnamed ordinary priests. Phinehas remains ordinary priest before Eleazar's death. Saul, David, Solomon, Samuel, Elijah and Elisha must not resemble supplied modern reference identities. Appropriate age follows each passage; never present a dead character as a living contemporary.
